title: Break down remediation
summary: Create independently reviewable outcomes in dependency order.

sections.label: Possible sequence
items: Characterize current behavior and its evidence.
Add a missing regression scenario where it is meaningful.
Implement a coherent correction or refactor.
Update the relevant decision and documentation.

sections.label: Scope
sections.text: Not every finding needs every stage. Distinguish behavior correction from structural cleanup when they need separate review.

sections.label: Acceptance
sections.text: Each task has a verifiable outcome and known dependencies, while the end-to-end scenario remains represented.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow steps: Stories and delivery plan. These links are recommendations based on the guide content, not required product or process choices.
A dependency list orders the proposed changes and identifies which can be independently reviewed.
Each change names one coherent outcome, its acceptance check and the evidence needed by its reviewer.
The combined plan retains an end-to-end scenario and any migration or rollback dependency. Intermediate states are checked for continued operation.

Only the added source contribution was fact checked in this pass. Earlier statements retain their original basis and confidence. Project configuration, usefulness and actual check outcomes remain unverified.

sections.label: Gap review: verified source contribution
sections.text: Google's published developer review guidance describes a self-contained change with related test code and recommends planning the split of dependent changes. The sequence in this guide remains a recommendation to adapt to the repository and reviewer. Checked against the linked primary source on 2026-10-15. This review covers this contribution only.

catalog.applicability: Use when a debt finding or correction is too large for one review and you need to split it into tasks in dependency order, each with a verifiable outcome, while the end-to-end scenario stays represented.
catalog.limits: Reading a topic does not configure tools, execute a workflow or establish passing evidence.
